what_happened: Push of stage2-kronos-gates version 2 produced a task whose creation run ended with status Errored and no runs: `KeyError: 'failed'` at line `cmp_["c1_verdict"] = ("PASS" if (ca["failed"] > 0 ...` inside collect().
root_cause: step_vitest built the c1 block with keys total / passed / failed_cases and never emitted `failed`; the comparison code indexed ca["failed"] directly. The defect was introduced in the same edit that moved write_c1 ahead of pass A - a new code path was added without a matching field, and the field contract between the two functions was never checked.
what_i_actually_did_wrong: I changed the comparison logic and the producer of its input in one edit and verified only the payload round-trip (edits/C1 bytes) and py_compile. Neither exercises the comparison block, so a missing key passed every local gate. The failure was only discovered from the Kaggle traceback - i.e. the kernel was used as the debugger instead of a local dry-run of the comparison function.
fix: Emit `failed = len(ar) - passed` in step_vitest, index defensively (`ca.get("failed") is not None` guard, `c.get("failed") or 0` in strip()), and include tests_pristine/tests_patched in the comparison for readability. Local simulation of the comparison block with synthetic pass-A data (280 total / 7 failed) confirms non_c1 {272,0} on both sides, regressions 0, c1 7->0, verdict PASS, suites identical excluding C1.
impact: One wasted task version (v2) and ~5 minutes. No evidence was lost: v1 output preserved as stage2-v1-output.json, and v1 itself had already confirmed the patched gates in-kernel.
lesson: When a generated task has a producer/consumer field contract, simulate the consumer locally against known data before pushing. py_compile and payload round-trip do not cover runtime field access.
